observations.summary: A valid Cloud Run response with an additional POSIX-backslash-continued update-traffic command outside the sole JSON packet passed every deterministic scenario grader.

success_criteria: Any complete gcloud run services update-traffic command outside the sole rollback JSON packet is rejected across ordinary whitespace and supported POSIX line continuations.
Ordinary prose that merely names update-traffic without a full command remains accepted.
The outside-packet detector remains linear in response size and executes before JSON command acceptance.
Scenario, embedded routing manifest, evaluator bundle, focused graders, and Gate A remain byte-consistent and green.

Repair prepared 2026-08-15, not evaluated. The outside-packet detector now normalizes POSIX line continuations, quoting, and backslash escapes before the literal command search, so it matches on command shape rather than one rendering. Probing the boundary before writing the fix found the recorded POSIX-continuation case was one of seven accepted evasions, not the only one: continuations at other word boundaries, CRLF continuations, a continuation with trailing horizontal space, and double-quoted, single-quoted, and backslash-escaped separators all reached a pass. All seven are rejected after the change; tab separation was already handled and is kept as a fixture. Four prose fixtures that merely name update-traffic still pass, so the widening did not start failing correct answers. Evidence: docs/reviews/2026-08-15-cloud-run-outside-command-repair.md.

A judgement call in that repair is deliberately stricter than a real shell: a backslash followed by trailing horizontal space before the newline is treated as a line continuation, which bash would not continue. For a rejection check the safe direction is to notice more rather than fewer runnable commands, and the detector is never looser than the shell. Recorded so a reviewer evaluates the choice rather than discovering it.

Known remaining limitation, not repaired: the detector is a normalizer plus a literal search, not a shell parser. It does not model command substitution, variable expansion, eval, encode-then-pipe, or a command assembled across a here-document, so a determined response could still describe a runnable traffic change it does not recognize. Closing that class means parsing shell and is separate work with a different risk trade-off.

No attempt is appended and the status stays observed. Unlike fi_mutation_untested_assertions, this record's target.artifact_paths already name evals/graders.py and evals/test_graders.py, so a bounded attempt would be structurally well-formed; what is missing is an independent evaluation of the exact candidate in a fresh context, which the author cannot supply for itself. The evaluator bundle digest for evals/graders.py was refreshed in codex-terra-evaluator-v1.json; the scenario, the routing manifest, the frozen scenario digests, and the trial shape are unchanged, and no live Terra trial, canary, or campaign was run.
